title: Red Light City
prompt: In my city, nobody can move when the traffic lights turn red. Not even inside their homes.

sheet.premise: In my city, nobody can move when the traffic lights turn red. Not even inside their homes.
sheet.rule: Everyone freezes on red, otherwise the lights find you.
sheet.whyObey: Nobody chooses to freeze. Your body just stops.
sheet.breakConsequence: People who move on red are never seen again.
sheet.beneficiary: Nova, the city controller, who sets the lights.
sheet.secret: The lights don't stop people. They stop time — for everyone except the controller.

protagonist.name: Bricks
protagonist.desire: To get my sister to the hospital in time.
protagonist.secret: I can move on red. I've never told anyone.

sheet.conflict: The lights turned red for an entire hour.
escalation: Then I saw someone else moving.
It was Nova, walking between the frozen people, taking things.
sheet.mystery: Why can I move when nobody else can?
sheet.twist: I can move on red because I'm the controller's daughter. He froze my mum the day I was born.
sheet.ending: He turned and looked straight at me. And smiled.
sheet.continuation: The light is about to turn green. I have ten seconds.

title: Everything Is Free
prompt: In my town, everything in the supermarket is free. But every item you take removes one memory.

sheet.premise: In my town, everything in the supermarket is free.
sheet.rule: Everyone can take whatever they want, but every item takes away one memory.
sheet.whyObey: It's the only food in town. Everyone pays eventually.
sheet.breakConsequence: Take too much and you forget who you are.
sheet.beneficiary: Nova, the store manager, who remembers everything.
sheet.secret: The memories aren't destroyed. They're being stocked on a shelf at the back.

protagonist.name: Bricks
protagonist.vulnerability: I'm running out of memories of our mum.
protagonist.secret: I've been paying for both of us.

sheet.conflict: I can't remember my mum's voice anymore.
sheet.mystery: Why does the back aisle hum when I walk past it?
sheet.twist: I broke into the back aisle and took my memories back. But they weren't all mine.
sheet.ending: I remember things that never happened to me. Things the manager did.
sheet.continuation: And now he knows exactly what I remember.

title: Classroom 13
prompt: Every classroom in my school has a number. Except classroom 13.

sheet.premise: Every classroom in my school has a number. Except one.
sheet.rule: Everyone must ignore the unnumbered door, otherwise they stop existing in photographs.
sheet.whyObey: Old yearbooks are full of empty spaces where kids used to be.
sheet.breakConsequence: You vanish from every photo. Then people start forgetting you.
sheet.beneficiary: Nova, the principal, who has worked here for sixty years and never aged.
sheet.secret: Classroom 13 isn't erasing students. It's keeping them.

protagonist.name: Juno
protagonist.desire: To prove my best friend was real.
protagonist.vulnerability: I'm the only one who still remembers him.
protagonist.secret: I have the last photo he's still in.

sheet.conflict: My best friend found the door.
escalation: He vanished from the class photo.
Then his mum asked me who I was talking about.
sheet.mystery: Why is the principal in every yearbook since 1960, looking exactly the same?
sheet.twist: The principal isn't guarding Classroom 13. He's its first student — and he's been looking for a replacement.
sheet.ending: The door has my number on it now. 13.
sheet.continuation: And my photo is starting to fade.

scenes.narration: This morning, the door had a number on it. Mine.

title: Lights Out at Nine
prompt: In my town, nobody is allowed to sleep before 9 PM.

sheet.premise: In my town, nobody is allowed to sleep before 9 PM.
sheet.rule: Everyone must stay awake until nine, otherwise they wake up in someone else's body.
sheet.whyObey: Nobody wants to wake up as a stranger.
sheet.breakConsequence: You wake up in a random body. Someone else wakes up in yours.
sheet.beneficiary: Sage, who runs the only all-night café and knows everyone's sleeping habits.
sheet.secret: The swaps aren't random. Someone has been choosing them.

protagonist.name: Dot
protagonist.desire: To get my own body back.

escalation: I woke up as Nova, the town's strictest teacher.
My real body was walking to school without me.
And it was being nicer to my friends than I ever was.
sheet.mystery: Why did it feel like the swap was waiting for me?
sheet.twist: Nobody stole my body. The person in it is who I'd be if I stopped being afraid.
sheet.ending: Tonight at nine, I can switch back. Or I can let them stay.
sheet.continuation: Which one of us should wake up tomorrow?

title: The Shadow Thief
prompt: In my town, lying is impossible. The moment you tell a lie, your shadow disappears.

sheet.premise: In my town, lying is impossible. The moment you tell a lie, your shadow disappears.
sheet.rule: Everyone must tell the truth, otherwise their shadow vanishes — and seven days later, so do they.
sheet.whyObey: Everyone has watched someone fade away.
sheet.breakConsequence: No shadow, then invisible to everyone after seven days.
sheet.beneficiary: Nova, the mayor, who has never lost his shadow.
sheet.secret: Nova isn't immune. He steals other people's shadows to hide his own lies.

protagonist.name: Bricks
protagonist.desire: To find out what happened to my dad.
protagonist.vulnerability: If I'm wrong about him, I lose the last good thing I believe.
protagonist.secret: I don't believe my dad ever lied.

sheet.conflict: My best friend lost her shadow. She swears she didn't lie.
escalation: Pixel lost her shadow, and she swears she never lied.
Then I noticed the mayor's shadow moves a second late.
Everyone in town says Nova has never told a lie. Not once.
sheet.mystery: How can a man who's never lied have the wrong shadow?
sheet.twist: The mayor isn't immune. He's been stealing other people's shadows to hide his own lies.
sheet.ending: I asked him where my dad was. He said: your father is the reason this town has a truth rule.
sheet.continuation: Then I looked down. My shadow was gone.

title: Don't Look at the Moon
prompt: In my town, nobody is allowed to look at the moon.

sheet.premise: In my town, nobody is allowed to look at the moon.
sheet.rule: Everyone must keep their eyes down at night, otherwise they disappear before sunrise.
sheet.whyObey: Every family has lost someone who looked.
sheet.breakConsequence: You're gone before sunrise. No body, no trace.
sheet.beneficiary: Nova, who keeps the town's curtains closed and the streets dark.
sheet.secret: The moon isn't taking people. It's calling them home.

protagonist.name: Pixel
protagonist.desire: To keep my little brother safe.
protagonist.vulnerability: He's all the family I have left.
protagonist.secret: I've seen him drawing the moon every night.

sheet.conflict: My little brother has been drawing the moon every night.
escalation: His drawings started appearing on everyone's windows.
Last night, they appeared on ours — from the outside.
Every drawing showed the same thing: our mother, standing on the moon.
sheet.mystery: Why does my brother know what our mother looked like? He was a baby when she left.
sheet.twist: The moon wasn't making people disappear. It was calling them home.
sheet.ending: Then my mother knocked on the window. She was outside, pointing up.
sheet.continuation: But my mother has been gone for twelve years.

scenes.narration: Anyone who looks at it disappears before sunrise. No body. No goodbye.
